## Case Study — Lemma Limited

Problem: Most short-form media never compounds. Creators publish without a hypothesis, get numbers back without a debrief, and make the next post the same way as the last one. The gap was operating discipline — not talent or distribution.

Research: Manual audience mapping across comments, save rates, watch-through curves, and share velocity. Treated each platform as a distinct market. Documented every test in a simple operating log capturing what was tried, what was expected, and what actually happened. Within 90 days could predict performance bands inside ±25%.

Execution: Weekly operating cadence. Every brief required three things: target audience, emotional takeaway, testable hypothesis. Killed about a third of backlog and doubled hit rate. Native-first cuts per platform with calibrated posting windows per audience timezone. Built a proto-fan-base CRM of most-engaged accounts.

Results: 10M+ cross-platform views. Repeatable operating engine. Documented playbook. Loyal returning audience. Inbound conversations with brands and artists who wanted to plug into the system.

Learnings:
1. Pick a smaller wedge earlier — generalist content is forgiving in month one and brutal by month six.
2. Build the measurement system on day one — clean metrics layer compounds.
3. Treat distribution as a product surface — platforms are distinct products with distinct users, not pipes.

## Case Study — PYR Studios

Problem: Southern California is dense with artists, independent musicians, and emerging brands, but short on the operating layer that turns raw talent into consistent output. Indie-tier talent was either DIYing and burning out, or getting priced into agency contracts that didn't fit their stage.

Research: Pre-launch listening tour with artists, managers, and brand owners across the region testing one hypothesis: was the gap in tools, in time, or in trust? Trust came up every time. Most clients had been burned by people who didn't understand their work or treated relationships as transactional.

Execution: Co-founded PYR with intentional Chula Vista positioning — close enough to San Diego and Tijuana to draw from both communities, far enough to be its own scene. Defined the service shape, sat in on client kickoffs, helped formalize working rhythms. Positioned as operating partner, not agency.

Results: Recognizable Chula Vista–based studio operating across artists, musicians, and brands. Highest signal of success: clients who came in for one engagement stayed for the next. Strong retention as a lagging indicator of model fit.

Learnings:
1. Customer research compounds — the listening tour was the highest ROI investment in the business; every later decision got cheaper because of it.
2. Positioning is a constraint, not a tagline — choosing "operating partner" over "agency" ruled out clients, services, and revenue shapes, which was the point.
3. Multi-stakeholder PM is its own skill — running a hub is closer to PM in a platform business than anything else.
